lessons.title: Calculating Measures of Center and Variability
addedFirstPartyContent: V12 optional-source-status correction: IM Algebra 1 Unit 1 Lesson 5 is an OPTIONAL BELOW-GRADE-LEVEL review. Before assigning it, an authorized teacher examines the pre-unit diagnostic: if students can already calculate mean, median, mean absolute deviation and IQR accurately, the lesson may be skipped. A skipped optional lesson is not a failed required academic standard, nor proof that an assessment was administered. Official teacher/student sources: https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/1/5/preparation.html and https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/1/5/index.html.

V12 original additional task: seven fictional measurements in minutes [3,5,5,7,9,9,11]. Their mean is7, median7, lower quartile5 and upper quartile9 under median-of-halves convention, IQR4 minutes, absolute deviations [4,2,2,0,2,2,4] and MAD16/7≈2.286 minutes. Plot dots and a correctly scaled number line. In pairs, explain why a median and MAD answer different questions. The official student activities include a physical meter-stick demonstration and heartbeat tables, but a text-only draft does not constitute an actually conducted demonstration.

V12 proposed teacher rubric (0–2 each, total8): original seven-point data plot and quartiles; correct mean, median, IQR and MAD with units; explanation and chosen quartile convention; genuine activity/diagnostic evidence if performed. Optional status must be respected in reporting.

criteria.name: Diagnostic optionality and conditional lesson assignment
Use of quartile/MAD definitions with units
Truthful actual physical demonstration and teacher observation

lessons.title: Writing Equations to Model Relationships (Part 1)
addedFirstPartyContent: V12 source-activity fidelity: the original student lesson combines mental percentages, vertex-edge-face relationships of solid figures, and progressively less-scaffolded contexts about income, spending and tax. In a warm-up compute25%,12%,8%,p% of 200; derive 50,24,16,2p. For a cube F=6,V=8,E=12 and tetrahedron F=4,V=4,E=6, verify V−E+F=2. This convex-solid relation is not claimed for arbitrary disjoint geometric assemblies. Teacher and student activity sources: https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/2/2/preparation.html and https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/2/2/index.html.

V12 independent sales scenario: a store charges $7 shipping after applying 8% sales tax to pre-tax goods cost x dollars. The model is T=1.08x+7. At x=$50, T=$61. If the shopper budget is $61, the constraint 1.08x+7≤61 gives x≤50 for nonnegative goods costs. Compare variable goods price x with fixed shipping7 and rate8%; a context may instead apply tax after shipping, creating a different model. Ask students to justify assumptions, not to memorize a single context-free equation.

Teacher human rubric 0–2 each for exact percentage calculations, correct polyhedral relationship and limits, clear fixed versus variable quantities/units, and a defensible tax/constraint equation with independent reasoning.

criteria.name: Tax constraint and peer assumption critique

lessons.title: Relative Frequency Tables
addedFirstPartyContent: V12 source-specific relative frequency representations: use the independent 40-response club table Group A [Sports12, Arts8] and Group B [Sports9, Arts11]. The JOINT table by grand total40 is A Sports30%, A Arts20%, B Sports22.5%, B Arts27.5%, whose cells sum100%. The ROW-CONDITIONAL tables are A [60%,40%] and B [45%,55%]; the COLUMN-CONDITIONAL tables are Sports [A12/21≈57.14%, B9/21≈42.86%], Arts [A8/19≈42.11%, B11/19≈57.89%]. Teacher and student sources: https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/3/2/preparation.html and https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/3/2/index.html.

V12 student task: draw three original segmented-bar representations from the separate joint, row and column percentages; label the reference populations and horizontal/vertical denominators. Explain why the percentages for A Sports differ (30%,60%,57.14%) without contradicting each other. The published unit includes segmented bars and a Notice and Wonder, so a frequency table alone does not complete its visual activity.

Draft teacher rubric0–2 each for joint-cell/whole sums, row/column denominators and totals, actual segmented bar graphs with labels, and contextual conditional probability reasoning. Visual learner artifact and teacher grading remain unverified.

criteria.name: Interpret a common cell in three reference groups

lessons.title: Function Notation
addedFirstPartyContent: V12 source-equivalent multi-function naming: the original source interprets three functions describing distance from a post over time, then introduces concise notation f(t),g(t),h(t). Use three independently invented probe models instead: f(t)=min(t,4) metres, g(t)=4−|t−3| metres, h(t)=2 metres for integer seconds t=0..6. At t=2, f(2)=2, g(2)=3, h(2)=2; at t=4, f(4)=4, g(4)=3, h(4)=2. Identical inputs can produce different outputs for DIFFERENT functions, without violating uniqueness within one named function. Source preparation/student: https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/4/2/preparation.html and https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/4/2/index.html.

V12 student task: match three original distance-time graphs to tables, name and use f, g and h, explain f(2)=2 metres in a sentence and compare it with g(2)=3 metres; translate one sentence into function notation and another back to the situation. Note the source expects interpretation from genuinely drawn graphs, so the existing one-function hiking calculation does not alone satisfy the activity.

Teacher draft rubric0–2 each for three correctly named function graph/table correspondences, input-output interpretation with units, meaning of multiple functions at same input, and student-authored notation/translation evidence.

criteria.name: Three distinct function graphs and corresponding tables
Named function uniqueness and cross-model comparisons

lessons.title: Patterns of Growth
addedFirstPartyContent: V12 source activity alignment: the official student lesson includes Which One Does Not Belong tables and spreadsheet-driven comparison of fixed increases versus fixed factors through TEN time steps. Extend independently authored tables A(t)=6+8t and B(t)=6×1.5^t from t0 through10. At t5, A=46 and B=45.5625; at t6 A=54 and B=68.34375, so B first exceeds A after their shared starting value at INTEGER step6. At t10 A=86 and B=345.990234375. Teacher/student: https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/5/2/preparation.html and https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/5/2/index.html.

V12 student tasks: create four source-equivalent original tables of constant additive, multiplicative and deliberately mixed differences with independent values, decide which does not belong with more than one defensible criterion, then create complete 11-row spreadsheet (t=0..10) for the two original function patterns. Explain why A(t+3)−A(t)=24 while B(t+3)/B(t)=1.5^3=3.375; include the exact operational formula and record real spreadsheet use only if performed.

Teacher review 0–2 each for table accuracy through t10, comparison of differences/factors over 1 and3 steps, correct representations of the crossover, and credible use of technology with explanation. Do not claim spreadsheet completion based on a JSON table.

criteria.name: Authentic spreadsheet work or clearly labeled manual substitute

requiredExactPractice: growth model table up to step10

lessons.title: How Does it Change?
addedFirstPartyContent: V12 source alignment: the original has a geometric diagram counting squares in different decompositions, visual dot-pattern comparisons of linear/exponential/quadratic change and student-produced graphs. Additional independent grid: a 7-by-9 rectangle with a missing 2-by-4 corner has area 63−8=55 unit squares. The same L-shaped figure can be decomposed into a 5-by-9 strip (45 squares) and a 2-by-5 strip (10 squares). This gives two expressions 7×9−2×4=5×9+2×5=55, justified by actual nonoverlapping regions; teacher/student: https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/6/2/preparation.html and https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/6/2/index.html.

V12 second visual task: invent first-party dot patterns L(n)=2n+1 (counts at steps0..4:1,3,5,7,9), Q(n)=n² (0,1,4,9,16) and E(n)=2^n (1,2,4,8,16). Draw each for n0..4, make an input/output table, graph each on a common scale and explain why first differences of Q are1,3,5,7, while E has fixed factor2. The squared term is a justified cell area, not merely a symbol. Avoid requiring rote formal equations in earlier unit6 lesson1.

Human rubric0–2 for valid L-shaped geometric decomposition, three actual diagrams and counts, graphs/tables with correct patterns, and explanation of quadratic squared-area term versus constant difference/factor.

criteria.name: Mathematical structure and squared term explanation

lessons.title: When and Why Do We Write Quadratic Equations?
addedFirstPartyContent: V12 source target correction: the publisher lesson explicitly contrasts contextual linear equations with quadratic equations, graph-estimation limitations and factored expression zeros. Additional original examples supplement the existing garden width model. Ticket price T(k)=9k+3 dollars for an integer number k of tickets; if total75 dollars, 9k+3=75 gives k8. An independent flight h(t)=−4t²+16t+12 metres reaches the ground when t²−4t−3=0, giving t=2±√7; only positive t=2+√7≈4.646s is physically valid and cannot be read exactly from a rough hand sketch. Teacher/student: https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/7/2/preparation.html and https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/7/2/index.html.

V12 first-party revenue task: R(p)=p(40−2p)=40p−2p² dollars, with feasible price0≤p≤20. Zeros are p0 and20. To obtain revenue128, solve p(40−2p)=128, giving p²−20p+64=0=(p−4)(p−16), hence prices4 or16. Maximum model revenue200 occurs at price10. Students compare which form makes zeros easy to read and explain why a graph estimate is insufficient for a precise irrational flight time.

Proposed teacher rubric0–2 each for appropriate equation creation and contextual variables, correct factored-root/linear comparison, graph limits/exact checks, and valid physical/economic domains. Human score and official approval remain pending.

criteria.name: Flight radical and graph estimation limitation

requiredExactPractice: teacher-reviewed context and physical roots; HUMAN_ONLY
